hints: Imagine pulling the list apart into two smaller chains as you walk it. Which chain does each node join, and how do you put them back together?
Two chains built in place: an odd chain starting at head and an even chain starting at head.next. Keep stitching each chain's tail to the node two ahead, then connect the odd tail to the even head.

1. If the list has fewer than 2 nodes, return it.
  2. Set odd = head, even = head.next, evenHead = even.
  3. While even != null and even.next != null: odd.next = even.next; odd = odd.next; even.next = odd.next; even = even.next.
  4. Attach odd.next = evenHead.
  5. Return head.

approaches.name: Copy values
approaches.idea: Collect odd-position then even-position values into an array and rebuild. Uses extra space.

approaches.name: Optimal: split into two chains in place
approaches.idea: Relink pointers to build both chains, then join them.

explain: For 10→20→30→40→50: the odd chain becomes 10→30→50 and the even chain 20→40. Finally 50 links to 20, giving 10→30→50→20→40. The loop condition makes sure the even pointer has a node after it; when it stops, odd is the last odd node. Remembering evenHead before the loop is essential, because head.next gets overwritten.
recognize: Rearrange nodes by position into groups while keeping order, with O(1) space → build separate chains in one pass and join them.
javascript: function oddEvenList(head) { const a = []; for (let c = head; c; c = c.next) a.push(c); const b = a.filter((_, i) => i % 2 === 0).concat(a.filter((_, i) => i % 2 === 1)); for (let i = 0; i < b.length; i++) b[i].next = b[i+1] || null; return b[0] || null; }
